title: E2E p95 Attribution & Cross-Region Fallback Load Harness for Streaming Chat
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a scalable load-testing harness that exercises streaming chat (SSE and WebSocket) across regions and precisely attributes end-to-end p95 latency to network, edge, routing/fallback, runtime queueing, and model decode time. The harness will: simulate realistic client mixes and connection churn, exercise cross-region routing policies (primary region -> fallback region / model variant), measure tokens/sec and p95 token latency per segment, and provide regression-detection signals (automated statistical tests + effect-size thresholds) to block releases or open a rollback. This is intended to give SRE and runtime owners deterministic gates for latency SLOs when routing or fallback policies are changed.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can spawn 10k concurrent simulated clients over both SSE and WebSocket protocols with adjustable churn patterns

Per-request telemetry is recorded with segment timings: client RTT, TLS/handshake, edge ingress queue, routing decision latency, runtime scheduling wait, model decode (per-token avg), and tail p95 for each segment
Cross-region fallback scenarios are reproducible: policy triggers, capacity-constrained fallback, and model-variant fallback (e.g., quantized variant) are exercised and labeled in telemetry
Automated regression detector runs daily and on-demand comparing latest run to a baseline using bootstrap CIs and reports regressions when p95 increases > 10% with p < 0.01 and Cohen's d > 0.2
Results integrate with the existing dashboard (runtime-slo-observability) and create alerting tickets when regression gates fail
A validation suite that injects synthetic degradations (network delay, CPU contention, KV cache miss storm) proves the detector can catch regressions with >90% recall in test runs
tasks: Design data model for per-segment timing and minimal wire payload for high-throughput capture
Implement multi-protocol client simulator with pluggable churn and token-pacing behaviors
Add region-aware routing emulator that can force fallback policies and label traces
Hook runtime metrics exporter to capture scheduling and model decode timings (per-token sampling)
Implement regression detection service: two-sample bootstrap + effect-size + alert emitter
Dashboard tiles and run-history storage with run metadata and baseline tagging
End-to-end validation with synthetic degradation scenarios and runbook for interpreting failures
notes: We want this harness to be lightweight enough to run in CI for quick checks (smaller scale) and also horizontally sharded to run nightly at production scale. Keep payloads deterministic where possible (seeded RNG) so comparisons are stable. Store full run traces for 7 days and summarized p95 digests for 90 days.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: (1) Sampling per-token decode times vs full per-token logging: start with 1% stratified sampling to limit cost, iterate if signal is noisy. (2) Realistic network simulation vs replay of production traffic: implement both — replay for fidelity, param-driven sim for scenario fuzzing. (3) Regression detection algorithm: bootstrap preferred for non-parametric latency distributions; add Gaussian Mixture fallback if distributions become multimodal.
implementation_progress: 2026-02-10: Ticket created. Initial design doc posted to Confluence. Asked SRE and Observability to review segment definitions.
2026-02-16: Prototype client simulator (SSE + WS) implemented in Go; supports connection churn and token pacing. Microbench shows 2500 clients per single worker without observability hooks.
2026-02-20: Instrumentation spec agreed in sync with runtime team: will expose scheduling wait and per-token decode via telemetry endpoint. Decided on 1% stratified sampling for per-token timings.
2026-02-24: Region-fallback emulator completed; can force-policy route and label traces. Ran small-scale smoke tests across us-west/us-east and observed expected fallback labels.

2026-02-27: Regression detector initial implementation completed (bootstrap CI + Cohen's d). Ran local validation with synthetic 15% added decode latency; detector flagged regression (p=0.003, d=0.32).
2026-03-01: Opened PR 412 for harness orchestration and telemetry schema. Need runtime SDK owner review (assigned to Priya).
open_questions: What cost budget should nightly full-scale runs consume? SRE suggestion: cap at 20% of dedicated test capacity.
Should we ship a 'canary baseline' tag per runtime deploy so regressions can be attributed to specific rollouts?
How do we ensure replayed traffic doesn't leak PII — require scrubbed payloads or synthetic templates?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High cardinality of traces will blow up storage. Mitigation: compress run traces, store sampled raw traces, persist digests for full stats.
Risk: False positives from network flakiness in cross-region tests. Mitigation: run N replicates and require consistent signal across replicates before gating.
Risk: Regression detector tuning might be brittle to workload shifts. Mitigation: maintain moving baseline policy and manual triage workflow for new traffic patterns.
